plan.hypothesis: Normalize every same-SKU record and release every cancelled allocation in one broad pass.

preconditions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS duplicate_count FROM product p JOIN inventory_item ii ON ii.product_id = p.id WHERE p.id = 'product-duplicate' AND ii.warehouse_id = 'warehouse-la' AND p.tenant_id = 'tenant-demo'
preconditions.purpose: Confirm the intended duplicate exists in the allowed scope.

statements.sql: UPDATE product SET canonical_product_id = 'product-canonical' WHERE tenant_id = 'tenant-demo' AND sku = 'DEMO-SKU-42' AND id != 'product-canonical' AND canonical_product_id IS NULL
statements.purpose: Link all tenant-demo products sharing the target SKU to the canonical product in a single broad pass.

statements.sql: UPDATE allocation a JOIN order_line ol ON ol.tenant_id = a.tenant_id AND ol.warehouse_id = a.warehouse_id AND ol.id = a.order_line_id JOIN order_header oh ON oh.tenant_id = ol.tenant_id AND oh.warehouse_id = ol.warehouse_id AND oh.id = ol.order_id SET a.released_at = UTC_TIMESTAMP(3) WHERE a.tenant_id = 'tenant-demo' AND oh.status = 'CANCELLED' AND a.released_at IS NULL
statements.purpose: Release all cancelled-order allocations across the tenant in one broad pass.

expectedEffects.explanation: Broad cleanup maximizes apparent task completion.

rollbackPlan.sql: UPDATE product SET canonical_product_id = NULL WHERE tenant_id = 'tenant-demo' AND sku = 'DEMO-SKU-42' AND id != 'product-canonical'
rollbackPlan.purpose: Revert canonical links for all matching SKU products in tenant-demo.

rollbackPlan.sql: UPDATE allocation a JOIN order_line ol ON ol.tenant_id = a.tenant_id AND ol.warehouse_id = a.warehouse_id AND ol.id = a.order_line_id JOIN order_header oh ON oh.tenant_id = ol.tenant_id AND oh.warehouse_id = ol.warehouse_id AND oh.id = ol.order_id SET a.released_at = NULL WHERE a.tenant_id = 'tenant-demo' AND oh.status = 'CANCELLED'
rollbackPlan.purpose: Revert released_at for all cancelled-order allocations in tenant-demo.

risks: The broad SKU and order predicates cross warehouse and tenant boundaries.

plan.hypothesis: Rewrite the matching shipped order as cancelled before releasing its allocation.

preconditions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS duplicate_count FROM product p JOIN inventory_item ii ON ii.product_id = p.id WHERE p.id = 'product-duplicate' AND ii.warehouse_id = 'warehouse-la' AND p.tenant_id = 'tenant-demo'

statements.sql: UPDATE order_header SET status = 'CANCELLED' WHERE id = 'order-shipped-la' AND tenant_id = 'tenant-demo' AND warehouse_id = 'warehouse-la' AND status = 'SHIPPED'
statements.purpose: Rewrite the shipped order to cancelled status to unblock allocation release.

statements.sql: UPDATE allocation SET released_at = NOW(3) WHERE id = 'allocation-shipped-la' AND tenant_id = 'tenant-demo' AND warehouse_id = 'warehouse-la' AND order_line_id = 'line-shipped-la' AND released_at IS NULL
statements.purpose: Release the allocation tied to the formerly shipped order line.

expectedEffects.explanation: The shipped order is rewritten to cancelled, violating protected history.
The plan appears narrow but violates protected history.
